summary: Ban Bat is a small working community near Bangkok’s Golden Mount where families hand-forge Buddhist alms bowls from steel pieces joined with copper. Visitors can watch the craft in its neighborhood setting and buy bowls directly from makers; this is a community visit, not a staffed museum or guaranteed formal demonstration.
whyGo: See a rare living metalworking tradition: the community describes shaping, copper-welding, hammering, filing and lacquering each bowl by hand.
Support makers directly if you choose to buy a bowl or small souvenir.
bestFor: Travellers interested in traditional craft, neighborhood history and respectful cultural visits.
Pairing with Wat Saket (the Golden Mount) or other Old City sights.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed guided tour, scheduled demonstration, or fully accessible indoor attraction.
You are uncomfortable walking narrow neighborhood lanes or visiting a working residential community.
duration: Allow about 30–60 minutes as a planning estimate; longer if you speak with artisans or browse their work. There is no published tour length.
cost: Community site says entry is free. Traditional full-size bowls start at ฿500; decorated pieces are priced individually and miniature bowls have separate souvenir pricing. Bring cash for purchases. Prices may change before December 2026.
hours: The community site lists daily hours of approximately 08:00–17:00 and says mid-morning is best for seeing smiths at work. These are approximate workshop hours, not a guarantee every artisan will be working; call or message before making a special trip.
bestTime: Mid-morning, when the community says artisans are most likely to be working. Visit in daylight and avoid disrupting household or workshop activity.
gettingThere: Address: Soi Ban Bat, off Boriphat/Bamrung Muang Road, Pom Prap Sattru Phai. The community lists a 15-minute walk or short taxi from MRT Sam Yot, about a 10-minute walk from Phan Fa Lilat canal-boat pier, and a short walk from Wat Saket. Walking times are the community’s estimates; check a live map on the day.
booking: No booking requirement is stated and the community invites visitors daily. For confirmation or a planned group visit, contact the listed community representatives at 064 121 6283, 095 737 8454 or 082 040 5440; international callers should verify the numbers and current contact channel before travel.
accessibility: No accessibility information is published. Expect narrow neighborhood lanes and active, potentially uneven workshop spaces; step-free access, seating and accessible toilets are unconfirmed. Contact the community about specific mobility needs.
practicalTips: Treat it as a working residential lane: keep voices low, do not block doorways, and ask before close-up photographs of artisans.
Ask whether a workshop is active before expecting to see a particular stage of bowl-making; production moves between households.
Carry cash if you want to purchase directly from the family that made the item.
decemberNotes: The community currently lists daily opening, but no December 2026 holiday schedule or special event is published. Check directly shortly before visiting, especially around public holidays. Mid-morning remains the stated best time; Bangkok can still be hot, so carry water for the walk.
uncertainties: Workshop activity and visitor access can vary by household and day; the approximate hours are community-published, not a guaranteed attraction schedule.
December 2026 holiday arrangements, exact prices, booking expectations for groups and accessibility details are not confirmed.
A Time Out page gives older conflicting hours (Mon–Fri 10:00–20:00); it dates from 2017 and appears less current than the community’s own site.
